heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

MAYOR OF PALEMBANG

PROVINCE OF SOUTH SUMATRA

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PALEMBANG CITY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. City is the City of Palembang.
2. City Government is the Government of the City of Palembang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Palembang.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the City Government.
5. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment is the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Community Empowerment of the City of Palembang.
6. Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA, is a Technical Implementation Unit established by the government to provide services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Women are all women who are both inside and outside the household.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Act of Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, or psychological to the victim.
10. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
11. Reporter is a person, family, and community who sees and hears that an act of violence has occurred against a woman or any woman who becomes a victim of an act of violence by another person.
12. Protection of Women and Children in Conflict with the Law is a form of service that must be carried out by law enforcement officers or security officers to provide a sense of security, both physical and psychological, to victims or witnesses from threats, disturbances, terror, and violence from any party given at the stage of investigation, inquiry, prosecution and examination at trial.
13. Protection .....
27. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children or blood relatives in a straight line upwards or downwards up to the third degree.
28. Family Resilience is the dynamic condition of a family that has tenacity and toughness and contains physical material and spiritual mental abilities to live independently and develop themselves and their families to live harmoniously in improving physical and spiritual welfare.
29. Community is a group of citizens who inhabit an official government administrative area (at the level of Neighborhood Association, Community Association, Village and Sub-district) and cooperate in life for a sufficiently long time and obey existing rules.
30. Religious Leaders consist of Ustadz/Ustadzah, Ulama, Pastors, Priests, Monks, Pedanda/Pandita/Sulinggih and other religious leaders who have gender sensitivity/awareness.
31. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy in order to provide strengthening and recovery of victims of violence as determined in a decision of an authorized official.

heading: Article 2
Article 3
Article 4
CHAPTER II
Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

1. The form of physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that physical violence is any act that results in pain according to medical experts, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.
2. The form of psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is that psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
3. The form of sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c is that sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, in an unnatural manner or disliked by one party for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. The form of neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is that neglect is the act of releasing and/or abandoning the responsibility of attention, care, education and livelihood towards every person who is a family member.
5. The form of exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is that exploitation is utilizing all forms of potential whether physical, psychological and intelligence in women or children for economic gain or personal pleasure of the perpetrator.

Paragraph 2

Paragraph 2

Community

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. Participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs against violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence to the competent authorities.
3. Monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
4. Small group units in society consisting of religious scholars, intellectuals, customary community units are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
5. Community Participation referred to in paragraph (1) means that community responsibility is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Family

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women and children is responsible for:
a. protecting women and children from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women and children;
b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and
c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Prevention

heading: Article 11
Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

In order to prevent violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the community:
a. plays an active role in monitoring various conditions occurring in its environment that may lead to violations of the rights of women and children;
b. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. prevents unregistered marriages and child marriages.

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

In order to prevent violations of the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the family:
a. protects women and children from various violations of rights in the household;
b. encourages the formation of a harmonious, educative, independent and fully responsible family; and
c. becomes a place for initial counseling and mediation for every family member suspected of violations of the rights of women and children.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Handling

heading: Article 14
Article 15
Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, families, the community and/or community organizations.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be made with complaints:
a. directly or direct findings;
b. by telephone or the like; and
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions are also authorized to handle women and children victims of acts of violence obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. Health services in handling women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 14 paragraph (1) letter b for women and children victims of acts of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 hours, of quality and carried out with maximum health service standards.
2. Women and children victims of acts of violence have the right to health services, including:
a. medical services;
b. medico-legal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
3. Medical services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, are in the form of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel.
4. Medico-legal services as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b, are a form of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the legal field.
5. Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. counseling services;
b. provision of safe houses;
c. spiritual guidance; and
d. economic recovery.
6. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), is organized by:
a. UPT PPA is tasked with carrying out technical operational activities in its working area in providing services for women and children victims of acts of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems;
b. the position of UPT PPA is under and responsible to the Head of the Office that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection at the city level; and
c. religious institutions.

heading: Article 21
Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

1. For social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 20 paragraph (2) letter b, the City Government may provide safe houses for women and victims of acts of violence in the form of intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
2. The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
3. The criteria for women and children victims of acts of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.
